rules.description: Every GST invoice must contain supplier name, address, GSTIN, consecutive serial number, date of issue, recipient details, HSN/SAC code, description, quantity, taxable value, tax rate, and total amount
rules.penalty_info: Rs. 10,000 per invoice or tax amount involved, whichever is higher under Section 122
rules.reference_section: Section 31 read with Rule 46 of CGST Rules 2017

rules.rule_name: HSN Code Requirement Based on Turnover
rules.description: Taxpayers with turnover up to Rs.5 crore must mention 4-digit HSN code; turnover above Rs.5 crore must mention 6-digit HSN code on B2B invoices
rules.penalty_info: Rs. 50,000 penalty under Section 125 for non-compliance
rules.reference_section: Notification No. 78/2020 - Central Tax dated 15th October 2020

rules.description: GSTIN must be 15 characters: first 2 digits are state code (01-37), next 10 characters are PAN, 13th is entity number, 14th is Z by default, 15th is checksum
rules.penalty_info: Invalid GSTIN renders the invoice non-compliant; ITC claim rejection

rules.description: GSTR-1 (outward supplies) must be filed by 11th of the following month for monthly filers, or by 13th of month following the quarter for QRMP scheme
rules.penalty_info: Late fee of Rs.50/day (Rs.20/day for nil return), maximum Rs.5,000 per return period

rules.description: GSTR-3B summary return must be filed by 20th of the following month. For QRMP taxpayers, by 22nd/24th of month following quarter
rules.penalty_info: Late fee Rs.50/day + 18% interest on tax liability from due date

rules.description: Input Tax Credit for any invoice must be claimed before 30th November of the following financial year or the date of filing annual return, whichever is earlier
rules.penalty_info: Permanent loss of ITC if not claimed within time limit

rules.description: If payment to supplier is not made within 180 days of invoice date, ITC claimed must be reversed with interest
rules.penalty_info: ITC reversal plus 18% interest from date of claim to date of reversal
rules.reference_section: Section 16(2) proviso, Rule 37 of CGST Rules

rules.description: E-Way Bill is mandatory for movement of goods exceeding Rs.50,000 in value (inter-state). States may have lower thresholds for intra-state movement
rules.penalty_info: Penalty of Rs.10,000 or tax sought to be evaded, whichever is greater. Goods and vehicle may be detained

rules.description: E-Way Bill validity: 200 km per day for regular cargo, 200 km per day for over-dimensional cargo. Must be generated before movement commences
rules.penalty_info: Detention of goods and vehicle; penalty under Section 129

rules.description: Composition scheme available for suppliers with aggregate turnover up to Rs.1.5 crore (Rs.75 lakh for special category states). Service providers up to Rs.50 lakh
rules.penalty_info: Automatic migration to regular scheme; back taxes with interest

rules.description: Composition dealers cannot collect tax from customers, cannot issue tax invoices, must issue Bill of Supply, and cannot claim ITC
rules.penalty_info: Rs.10,000 or tax amount, whichever is higher under Section 122

rules.description: Recipient must pay GST under RCM for specified goods/services (e.g., legal services from advocates, transportation by GTA, import of services)
rules.penalty_info: Tax amount plus 18% interest; penalty up to 100% of tax under Section 73/74
rules.reference_section: Section 9(3) and 9(4) of CGST Act 2017, Notification 13/2017

rules.description: Every registered person must file annual return in GSTR-9 by 31st December of the following financial year. Turnover above Rs.5 crore requires GSTR-9C reconciliation statement
rules.penalty_info: Late fee of Rs.200/day (Rs.100 CGST + Rs.100 SGST), max 0.5% of turnover

rules.description: E-invoicing is mandatory for businesses with aggregate turnover exceeding Rs.5 crore. Invoice Reference Number (IRN) must be generated on Invoice Registration Portal
rules.penalty_info: Invoice treated as invalid; ITC denial to recipient; penalty Rs.10,000 per invoice
rules.reference_section: Notification No. 13/2020, Rule 48(4) of CGST Rules

rules.description: Government entities and specified persons must deduct TDS at 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST/UTGST) on payments exceeding Rs.2.5 lakh to suppliers
rules.penalty_info: Interest at 18% on delayed deduction; late filing fee

rules.description: Credit notes must be issued before 30th November of the following financial year or date of filing annual return, whichever is earlier
rules.penalty_info: Cannot reduce tax liability after time limit; excess tax paid becomes irrecoverable

rules.description: Personal data shall be processed only for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given consent. Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous with clear affirmative action
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.250 crore per instance
rules.reference_section: Section 4 and Section 6 of DPDP Act 2023

rules.description: Data Fiduciary must give a notice in clear plain language containing: description of data, purpose, manner to exercise rights, and grievance mechanism
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.200 crore

rules.description: Personal data may be transferred outside India except to countries notified by Central Government as restricted. Significant Data Fiduciaries may have additional restrictions
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.250 crore

rules.description: Data Fiduciary must notify the Data Protection Board of India of any personal data breach without delay. Must also inform affected Data Principals
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.200 crore for failure to notify

rules.description: Data Principal has the right to obtain summary of personal data being processed, processing activities, identities of other Data Fiduciaries with whom data has been shared
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.200 crore for non-compliance with rights

rules.description: Data Principal has the right to correction of inaccurate/misleading data, completion of incomplete data, updating of data, and erasure of data no longer needed
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.200 crore

rules.description: Personal data collected for one purpose cannot be processed for another purpose without separate consent. Data must be used only for the purpose communicated in the consent notice

check_params.check_prompt: Verify if the document indicates data usage beyond the stated purpose of collection

rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.250 crore

rules.description: Personal data shall be retained only for the period necessary for the stated purpose. Must be erased when purpose is fulfilled or consent is withdrawn, unless retention required by law
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.200 crore

rules.description: Processing personal data of children (below 18 years) requires verifiable consent of parent/guardian. Tracking, behavioral monitoring, and targeted advertising directed at children is prohibited
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.200 crore

rules.description: Significant Data Fiduciaries must appoint DPO based in India, conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments, conduct periodic audits, and publish contact info of DPO
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.150 crore

rules.description: Every Data Fiduciary must establish an accessible grievance redressal mechanism and respond to Data Principal grievances within prescribed timelines
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.200 crore

rules.description: Listed entities must disclose material events/information within 24 hours or 30 minutes (for certain events) to stock exchanges. Includes board meeting outcomes, financial results, mergers
rules.penalty_info: Fine up to Rs.25 crore; trading suspension possible

rules.description: Listed entities must disclose shareholding pattern within 10 days from end of each quarter to stock exchanges in prescribed format
rules.penalty_info: Fine of Rs.5,000/day of non-compliance

rules.description: No insider shall trade in securities when in possession of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI). Insiders must not communicate UPSI except for legitimate purposes

check_params.check_prompt: Check if document contains references to trading while in possession of material non-public information

rules.penalty_info: Penalty of Rs.25 crore or 3x profit made, whichever is higher. Criminal prosecution possible
rules.reference_section: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations 2015, Regulation 3 & 4

rules.description: Trading window must be closed for designated persons from end of quarter till 48 hours after declaration of financial results. Code of conduct must be maintained
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.25 crore per violation

rules.description: Listed entities must submit quarterly unaudited financial results within 45 days from end of quarter, and annual audited results within 60 days from end of financial year
rules.penalty_info: Fine and possible trading suspension; freeze on promoter holdings

rules.description: Board must have optimal combination of executive and non-executive directors. At least one-third must be independent directors. Woman director mandatory for top 1000 listed entities
rules.penalty_info: Fine up to Rs.5 lakh per day of non-compliance

rules.description: Audit committee must have minimum 3 members, two-thirds must be independent directors, chairperson must be independent director with financial literacy
rules.penalty_info: Fine; possible delisting proceedings

rules.description: All related party transactions must have audit committee approval. Material RPTs require shareholder approval. Related parties cannot vote on such resolutions
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.25 crore; transaction may be voided

rules.description: Any person acquiring 5% or more shares must disclose to company within 2 working days. Any change of 2% or more must be disclosed
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.25 crore

rules.description: Quarterly corporate governance compliance report must be submitted to stock exchanges within 15 days from end of quarter
rules.penalty_info: Fine up to Rs.5,000/day

rules.description: Listed entities must resolve investor grievances within 15 days. Must file statement of investor complaints with exchanges on quarterly basis
rules.penalty_info: Fine; SEBI SCORES escalation

rules.description: Banks and regulated entities must perform Customer Due Diligence at account opening. Must verify identity using OVDs (Officially Valid Documents): Passport, Driving License, Voter ID, Aadhaar, NREGA Card
rules.penalty_info: Penalty up to Rs.5 crore on regulated entity; criminal prosecution under PMLA

rules.description: KYC must be updated periodically: every 2 years for high-risk, every 8 years for medium-risk, and every 10 years for low-risk customers. Video KYC (V-CIP) permitted for re-KYC
rules.penalty_info: Account restrictions; regulatory penalty on institution
rules.reference_section: RBI Master Direction on KYC, Section 38

rules.description: Every NBFC with asset size Rs.500 crore or above is categorized as NBFC-Upper Layer. All NBFCs must be registered with RBI to conduct financial business
rules.penalty_info: Criminal prosecution; penalty up to Rs.5 crore
rules.reference_section: RBI Scale Based Regulation (SBR) Framework, October 2022

rules.description: NBFCs must maintain minimum CRAR of 15% with Tier-I capital minimum 10%. NBFC-Upper Layer must maintain 9% CET-1
rules.penalty_info: Restrictions on business; possible cancellation of certificate of registration
rules.reference_section: RBI Master Direction for NBFCs, Chapter IV

rules.description: Digital lenders must disclose APR (all-inclusive cost), loan agreement via KFS (Key Fact Statement) before loan execution. Must provide cooling-off period for borrower exit
rules.penalty_info: Regulatory action against lending entity; possible ban on digital lending operations
rules.reference_section: RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending, September 2022

rules.description: First Loss Default Guarantee (FLDG) provided by LSPs/DLAs to REs capped at 5% of loan portfolio. FLDG arrangements must be backed by cash/fixed deposits
rules.penalty_info: Cancellation of arrangement; regulatory action
rules.reference_section: RBI Circular on FLDG in Digital Lending, June 2023

rules.description: All payment aggregators must obtain authorization from RBI. Net worth requirement of Rs.25 crore by specified deadline. Must maintain escrow account with scheduled commercial bank
rules.penalty_info: Shutdown of operations; penalty under Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007
rules.reference_section: RBI Guidelines on Payment Aggregators and Gateways, March 2020 (amended 2024)

rules.description: Payment aggregators must store payment data only in India. Card data (full card number, CVV, expiry) must not be stored. Tokenization mandatory for card storage
rules.penalty_info: Authorization revocation; penalty under IT Act and PSS Act
rules.reference_section: RBI Circular on Card-on-File Tokenization, September 2021

rules.description: Regulated entities must file STRs with FIU-IND within 7 days of suspicion. CTRs for cash transactions above Rs.10 lakh in a month must be filed
rules.penalty_info: Penalty under PMLA Section 13; up to Rs.5 lakh per transaction
rules.reference_section: PMLA Act 2002, RBI Master Direction on KYC

rules.description: Regulated entities must resolve customer complaints within 30 days. If unresolved, customer can approach RBI Ombudsman. Internal ombudsman mandatory for entities with 10+ branches
rules.penalty_info: Regulatory penalty; adverse supervisory action

rules.description: Banks must achieve 40% of ANBC as priority sector lending. Sub-targets: Agriculture 18%, Micro Enterprises 7.5%, Weaker Sections 12%
rules.penalty_info: Shortfall to be deposited in RIDF/other funds at below-market rates
rules.reference_section: RBI Master Direction on Priority Sector Lending, 2020

rules.description: Every company must hold minimum 4 board meetings per year with not more than 120 days gap between two consecutive meetings. One Person Company requires minimum 1 meeting per half year
rules.penalty_info: Fine on company Rs.25,000 and on every officer in default Rs.5,000

rules.description: Quorum is one-third of total strength or 2 directors, whichever is higher. For interested directors, they are not counted in quorum for that agenda item
rules.penalty_info: Decisions taken without quorum are void

rules.description: Every company must file annual return in Form MGT-7 within 60 days from the date of AGM. OPC and small companies file MGT-7A
rules.penalty_info: Additional fee Rs.100/day; penalty Rs.10,000 to Rs.5,00,000 on company; Rs.50,000 to Rs.5,00,000 on officer

rules.description: Every company must file financial statements in Form AOC-4 within 30 days of AGM. Consolidated statements in AOC-4 CFS. XBRL filing mandatory for specified companies
rules.penalty_info: Additional fee Rs.100/day; penalty on company and officers

rules.description: AGM must be held within 6 months from close of financial year (by 30th September). Gap between two AGMs must not exceed 15 months. First AGM within 9 months of closure of first FY
rules.penalty_info: Fine up to Rs.1 lakh on company; Rs.5,000/day on officers

rules.description: Every person appointed as director must have a DIN allotted by MCA. Application in DIR-3 or SPICe+ at incorporation. DIN is unique and valid for lifetime
rules.penalty_info: Appointment void if DIN not obtained; penalty on individual Rs.5,000/day

rules.description: A person cannot hold directorship in more than 20 companies at a time, of which not more than 10 can be public companies. Independent directors limited to 7 listed companies
rules.penalty_info: Fine Rs.5,000/day on person continuing excess directorship

rules.description: Listed companies and companies with paid-up capital Rs.100 crore or turnover Rs.300 crore must have at least one woman director
rules.penalty_info: Fine Rs.1 lakh to Rs.5 lakh on company; Rs.25,000 to Rs.1 lakh on officer
rules.reference_section: Section 149(1) proviso, Rule 3 of Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014

rules.description: Companies with net worth Rs.500 crore or turnover Rs.1000 crore or net profit Rs.5 crore must spend 2% of average net profit of preceding 3 years on CSR activities
rules.penalty_info: Unspent amount to be transferred to Fund within 6 months. Non-compliance: fine 2x unspent or Rs.1 crore; officers Rs.1/10th or Rs.2 lakh

rules.description: Auditor appointed for 5-year term (individual) or 10-year term (firm). Mandatory rotation for listed and prescribed companies. Cooling-off period of 5 years post rotation
rules.penalty_info: Appointment treated as casual vacancy; penalty on company and auditor

rules.description: Every listed company and every company with paid-up share capital of Rs.10 crore or more must appoint a whole-time company secretary
rules.penalty_info: Fine up to Rs.5 lakh on company

rules.description: Employer must contribute 12% of basic wages + DA to EPF for employees earning up to Rs.15,000/month. Must file ECR (Electronic Challan cum Return) by 15th of following month
rules.penalty_info: Damages up to 100% of arrears; imprisonment up to 3 years under Section 14 of EPF Act
rules.reference_section: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952, Section 6

rules.description: Applicable to establishments with 10+ employees (20 in some states). Employee earning up to Rs.21,000/month covered. Employer contributes 3.25%, employee 0.75%
rules.penalty_info: Damages up to 25% of contribution; imprisonment up to 2 years

rules.description: Every employer must pay at least the minimum wages fixed by appropriate government for scheduled employment. Wages vary by state, skill level, and zone
rules.penalty_info: Fine up to Rs.50,000; repeat offence: imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs.1 lakh
rules.reference_section: Code on Wages 2019, Section 54 (earlier: Minimum Wages Act 1948)

rules.description: Gratuity payable to employees on termination/retirement/death after 5 years of continuous service. Amount: 15 days wages for each completed year. Maximum Rs.25 lakh
rules.penalty_info: Simple interest on delayed payment; fine up to Rs.1 lakh or imprisonment up to 2 years

rules.description: Applicable to establishments with 20+ employees. Minimum bonus 8.33% of wages (even if no profits). Maximum 20%. Payable to employees earning up to Rs.21,000/month
rules.penalty_info: Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs.1 lakh

rules.description: Employer must deduct professional tax from employees' salary as per state slab rates and remit to state government. Maximum Rs.2,500 per year. Not applicable in all states
rules.penalty_info: Interest on delayed payment; penalty varies by state
rules.reference_section: Article 276 of Constitution; respective State PT Acts

rules.description: Maximum 48 hours per week (under new Code: 8 hours/day with 4 days week option). Overtime payable at 2x normal wages. Annual leave: 1 day for every 20 days worked
rules.penalty_info: Fine up to Rs.1 lakh for first offence; Rs.2 lakh for subsequent
rules.reference_section: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020, Section 25-27

rules.description: No discrimination in wages on grounds of gender for same work or work of similar nature. Applies to recruitment, training, and promotions as well

check_params.check_prompt: Verify if pay structure shows gender-based discrimination for similar roles

rules.penalty_info: Fine Rs.50,000; repeat offence: imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs.1 lakh
rules.reference_section: Code on Wages 2019, Section 3 (earlier: Equal Remuneration Act 1976)
